content.text: Found FeVO4 (MACE hull 0, HSE gap 2.75 eV). Now I'll record the required consultation and take the first merit measurement in the dense V-rich region.

input.verdict: Weak support: FeVO4 is on the hull (MACE) but its HSE gap 2.75 eV exceeds the 2.4 eV photons, so pure FeVO4 would absorb poorly. The Cu content in V-rich films should add Cu vanadate phases with smaller gaps, so this measurement checks the densely sampled V-rich region as a baseline.

input.verdict: Support: replacing Fe with Cu in the FeVO4 structure brings the predicted HSE gap down to about 1.15 eV. Films richer in Cu should therefore absorb 2.4 eV light much better than V-rich/FeVO4-like films. Measuring Cu-rich index 127 (Cu:V ~1.5, near Cu3V2O8, with some Fe) tests this. The structure is hypothetical, so this is a qualitative trend, not a value.

content.text: Index 127 (Cu-rich, 9.6e-7 A) gave 2.5× the photocurrent of index 19 (V-rich). I'll get one more model receipt, then use the last measurement to test adding Fe at the same Cu:V ratio.

input.verdict: Mixed but supports staying Cu-rich. A Cu analog of the FeVO4 structure sits 0.112 eV/atom above the hull, so Cu should form its own Cu vanadates (e.g. Cu3V2O8) instead of entering the FeVO4 structure. Fe is likely present as a stable FeVO4-type co-phase or as an alloying element. Index 128 keeps the same Cu:V ratio as the best result so far (index 127, ~0.59) and adds a little Fe (0.22). This tests whether more Fe helps the Cu3V2O8-like phase.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 127** (Cu 0.50, Fe 0.17, V 0.33) as the best composition. At 9.6e-7 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, but three points in a 297-composition library can't show it's the best one in the library.

| Index | Cu / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | 0.10 / 0.105 / 0.79 | 3.8e-7 |
| **127** | **0.50 / 0.17 / 0.33** | **9.6e-7** |
| 128 | 0.46 / 0.22 / 0.32 | 8.5e-7 |

**Why I chose these three:**
- **Index 19:** a baseline in the densely sampled V-rich region. FeVO4 is stable according to the machine-learned stability model (MACE), but the band-gap model (MEGNet) puts its gap at 2.75 eV, above the 2.4 eV light, so it would absorb poorly.
- **Index 127:** putting Cu in place of Fe in the FeVO4 structure dropped the predicted gap to about 1.15 eV. That pointed me towards Cu-rich films, and 127 gave 2.5× the photocurrent of index 19. This is a hypothetical structure that is predicted to be unstable (0.112 eV/atom above the hull), so it only suggests a trend.
- **Index 128:** kept the same Cu:V ratio as 127 with a bit more Fe. It came out slightly lower, so adding Fe didn't help there.

**Gaps you should know about:**
- The phase list was too large to return, so it went to a file I couldn't read. The only real phase I checked was FeVO4 (mp-504509), which I found by guessing its ID.
- I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I haven't confirmed which phases are actually in the films.
- I didn't measure the Fe-rich region or the most Cu-rich corner (Cu about 0.65), so a better composition could be in either.
